title: The Sexy Pirate Book
logline: On a road trip to Atlantic City, Lily turns her forty dollars of budgeted fun money into six thousand by beating Barney at the one game nobody understands, then tries to hide the windfall from Marshall while wearing the worst hiding place in New Jersey: Barney's jacket.

guests.name: Desmond
guests.role: The only dealer in Atlantic City who knows all six hundred pages of Xing Hai Shi Bu Xing. Courtly and mournful, he has dealt Barney four hundred and twelve hands and waited thirty-one years for someone who read the book.

facts.marshall.budget: Eriksen Envelope System with Lily; windfalls go to the Nest Egg
facts.lily.studio: rented a painting studio over an Avenue B dry cleaner for one year
facts.barney.gamerecord: Xing Hai Shi Bu Xing: 412 wins, 10 losses (first loss to Lily)
facts.barney.dealer: Desmond deals his Xing Hai Shi Bu Xing table in Atlantic City
facts.lily.jacket: won Barney's charcoal suit jacket at the table and kept it
facts.ted.fireplace: Lily's painting of the drive home from Atlantic City hangs over it in 2030

opens.note: Barney wants a Xing Hai Shi Bu Xing rematch against Lily; she has started a rematch envelope

scenes.summary: The drive down. Marshall's sandwich cooler has taken shotgun, so Ted, Robin and Lily share the back. Marshall hands out the Eriksen Envelope System and dodges the Miscellaneous line. Barney, at the table with Desmond since Wednesday, calls in to brag 412 and oh. Lily lies about her book.

beats.line: Barney got to Atlantic City three days before the rest of us. He said he needed to stretch.
Remind me why I'm in the middle seat.
Because a cooler called shotgun.
That cooler is carrying sixty dollars of homemade sandwiches, Ted. It wears a seatbelt.
I called shotgun in March. It's a standing reservation.
And you lost it to a ham.
Okay, people! This weekend, Lily and I are on the Eriksen Envelope System.
I'm the envelope guy. He gave me an envelope full of envelopes.
Lily, fun money, forty dollars. Marshmallow, it's Atlantic City. Forty dollars is one shrimp cocktail.
Then it's going to be a very special shrimp.
And if she wins?
Rule one. Windfalls go to the Nest Egg.
Rule two. No secret windfalls. Eriksens tell each other everything.
Everything. Love it. Big fan of rule two.
Hey, what's this on the back? Miscellaneous, twenty dollars a week?
Miscellaneous is miscellaneous, Lily. That's the beauty of it.
Actually, that's the definition of a—
Ted. Shotgun gets opinions. Back seat gets sandwiches.
Ted! Where are you? Desmond and I have been warming up since Thursday.
Wednesday, sir.
Four hundred and twelve hands of Xing Hai Shi Bu Xing. Four hundred and twelve and oh.
Name one rule.
When the dealer taps the table twice, everybody stands up.
Why?
Respect.
There's an official rulebook. Six hundred pages. I tried to read it once. Page one is just a warning.
Never read it, Ted. That's my secret. You can't lose a game you don't understand.
So far, sir.
Speaking of reading. Lilypad, you've had your nose in that book for three weeks. What is it?
It's a sexy pirate book.
What's the pirate's name?
Captain... Page Four Hundred.

scenes.summary: Barney introduces Desmond. Marshall leaves for the penny slots. Lily buys in with her forty dollars, asks Desmond to tap twice, and the pirate book is revealed as the rulebook. She takes Barney apart, wins six thousand dollars and his jacket, and realizes rule one. Robin and Ted bet the hump on whether she tells Marshall before they leave town.

beats.line: Finally! Guys, Desmond. He's dealt every one of my four hundred and twelve wins.
Desmond, tell them how much you look forward to my visits.
Every year, Mister Stinson. Like taxes.
Desmond, honestly. Does Barney understand the rules?
Mister Stinson and the rules have never been introduced.
Drinks are free while you're playing. I put one quarter in a slot machine an hour ago. Officially, I'm still playing.
Okay! Penny slots, second floor. Forty dollars, four hours. That's seventeen cents of fun a minute.
You coming, Lilypad?
Go ahead, baby. I want to watch Barney do his little thing.
Deal me in, Desmond. Forty dollars.
Lily, this isn't a game for amateurs. Or professionals. It's a game for me.
Madam. Have you read the book?
Desmond, you haven't tapped twice yet.
Thirty-one years. Nobody has ever asked me to tap.
Out of respect!
It's so he can count the players, Barney.
It was not a sexy pirate book.
Lilypad? It's three in the morning.
The pirate just took his shirt off.
Okay. Don't let him get cold.
Rule two-twelve. Wind tiles count double on Saturdays. Barney, you idiot.
The usual, Desmond. Everything on the moon tile.
Madam?
West wind under the moon. And it's a Saturday.
Rule two hundred and twelve. Madam wins.
That's not a rule!
Page one hundred nineteen, sir.
She beat him again. And again. Barney kept doubling his bet, because he had never once experienced the alternative.
Ted, what's this feeling in my chest?
That's losing.
Double or nothing. Everything I've got. Plus the jacket.
Barney, not the jacket! Without it you're just a guy!
Barney, the pot is six thousand dollars. That jacket is worth maybe fifty.
This jacket is worth more than Desmond's car.
It is.
East wind. Doubled. Saturday.
Madam wins.
Six thousand two hundred and forty dollars. And one jacket.
Lily! You beat Barney!
Your forty dollars, madam. It brought friends.
Six thousand dollars! Wait till Marshall—
Windfalls go to the Nest Egg.
Okay. Nobody tells Marshall.
Ted, she tells him before we leave Atlantic City. Loser rides the hump home.
Lily's a vault. You're on.
I'm standing right here!
Lily, I love you. But your face is terrible at this.
Four hundred and twelve and one.

scenes.summary: Lily hides the money in Barney's jacket. Marshall comes back up eleven cents; Lily overcompensates, the thermostat lies collide, Ted calls it passive solar, Robin texts Marshall a tip for the hump, and Barney lies about his record to protect himself, which protects her. Barney's rematch threat dies; Lily hands him the rulebook.

beats.line: Your Aunt Lily had been rich for eleven minutes. She had already found the worst hiding place in New Jersey.
You're wearing Barney's jacket. That's not hiding. That's a confession with lapels.
It has an inside pocket. Marshall reorganizes my purse every Sunday. He labels the gum.
And you just handed it over?
That jacket watched me lose, Ted. I can never wear it again.
Incoming.
Guys! Two hours on the penny slots and I am up eleven cents!
Marshmallow! Hi! I didn't win anything!
How were the slots? I also didn't win anything.
Why are you wearing Barney's jacket?
I'm cold.
Lily, casinos are kept at exactly sixty-eight degrees to keep you awake and gambling. I read the pamphlet.
I'm a cold person, Marshall!
And Barney, where's your jacket?
Resting.
Marshall, it's simple. Lily runs cold, Barney runs hot. They're sharing heat. It's passive solar design.
Then what's the sun?
Barney is the sun.
Thank you.
Robin says to check the jacket pocket.
Robin!
Three hours in the hump, Ted. My spine is shaped like New Jersey.
There's nothing in the pocket. That's what pockets are for. Nothing.
Ooh, then can I borrow it? I want to do my Barney.
No!
You love my Barney.
So how'd it go? Four hundred and thirteen and oh?
Four hundred and thirteen and oh. Obviously.
Awesome. I'm hitting the buffet. I budgeted for one plate, so I'm going to build it very, very high.
Rematch. Right now. Or I tell him everything.
Tell him what, Barney? That you lost?
We will never speak of this.
You want a rematch so bad? Start here.
Page one. Do not play this game against anyone who has read this book.

scenes.label: 2:40 AM
scenes.summary: After hours at the empty gaming table, Robin is about to collect on the bet. Lily tells her what the money is for: a studio, and the fear that Marshall will look at it and see the shoes. Robin tells her to go show him, and enjoys that she wins either way.

beats.line: Six hours, four dollars, eleven scotches. I'm basically beating the house.
Robin, please don't tell Marshall.
Then tell me why I should ride the hump for you.
There's a studio on Avenue B. Over a dry cleaner.
A painting studio?
Four hundred a month. And it has a window.
A window? In Manhattan? Who did you have to kill?
Six thousand dollars is fifteen months of me being a painter again.
So tell him. He'd love that.
Robin, we have a budget because of me. My credit cards. My shoes.
Every envelope has a job. Rent, loans, Nest Egg. There isn't one envelope that's just me wanting something.
The last time I hid money from Marshall, it was a credit card bill. This feels exactly the same. Except I won.
Drink.
I've had a secret bank account since I was sixteen. The Get Out of Town Fund. It's in a hockey bag.
I don't want to get out of town. I want him to want this for me.
I'm just scared he'll look at it and see the shoes.
Then go show him it's not shoes.
You'd win the bet.
I know. It's a beautiful moment for both of us.
Okay. Okay. That's a full hug.

scenes.summary: Lily finds Marshall at the empty Xing Hai table and tells him everything. Marshall reclassifies the windfall as wages, then confesses Miscellaneous: two years of twenty dollars a week, saved for her studio. Quiet kiss.

beats.line: Hey. I saved you the special shrimp.
Marshall, I have to tell you something. And I need you to not do math until I'm done.
I'll try. Sometimes it just happens.
I beat Barney at Xing Hai Shi Bu Xing. That's six thousand two hundred and forty dollars.
You beat Barney?
I've been studying the rulebook for three weeks.
So there's no pirate.
There's no pirate. There's a sixty-year-old dealer named Desmond.
Oh, thank God. I was so jealous of that guy.
I was going to hide it. There's a studio on Avenue B. I want to paint again. And there's no envelope for that.
Rule one. Windfalls go to the Nest Egg.
I know.
But a windfall is money that falls on you.
You read six hundred pages at three in the morning. That's not a windfall, Lily. That's wages.
Did you just lawyer our budget?
I lawyered our budget.
Also. I need to tell you about Miscellaneous.
Twenty dollars a week.
For two years. Two thousand and eighty dollars. It says Lily's studio on the front.
I was going to give it to you on your birthday.
How did you even know?
Baby, you've drawn that dry cleaner on every napkin at MacLaren's.
And you kept it a secret for two years?
Lily, I'm a great secret keeper.
Since when?
Since I married the worst one in the world.

scenes.summary: The drive home. Lily rides up front with Marshall. Ted lost the bet and sits in the hump of an otherwise empty back seat, because a bet's a bet. Robin stayed behind to watch Barney, who calls: he read the whole book and now he loses. Lily asks for one more envelope. Future Ted reveals where the night ended up: over his fireplace.

beats.line: Ted, buddy. There are two empty seats back there.
A bet's a bet, Marshall. I lost the hump fair and square.
Even though you didn't crack. You chose. Those are two completely different things.
Ted, Robin's not even here. She can't see you.
Ted. Are you in the middle seat?
Yes, Robin.
Good.
How's Barney?
I stayed to watch him lose. Best decision I've ever made.
Lily. I stayed up all night. I read the book.
All six hundred pages.
I finally understand Xing Hai Shi Bu Xing.
And?
Four hundred and twelve and nine.
Ten, sir.
Marshmallow? Can we add one more envelope to the budget?
What's it for?
Barney's going to want a rematch. I'm going to need a bigger envelope.
Aunt Lily kept that studio for one year. She painted nineteen pictures. By her count, eighteen are terrible.
The nineteenth hangs over our fireplace. You two have walked past it your whole lives.
A car at dawn. Three people, two empty seats, and me in the middle for no reason at all.
